evidence: STATUS_BY_KIND maps ErrorKind values to HTTP status codes. This is a transport concern, so it belongs in infrastructure.
clientHttpStatus checks the status/expose properties of errors raised by Express. This is framework-specific logic, so it belongs in infrastructure.
notFoundHandler and errorHandler are Express middleware that build JSON HTTP responses. This is transport/presentation adapter work.
errorHandler calls classifyError(error) from the application layer to classify the error, so no business classification is done inside the infrastructure file.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is Express HTTP transport middleware, and it sits in the infrastructure layer. It handles transport concerns: it maps error kinds to HTTP status codes, recognizes client errors raised by Express (status/expose), replies with 404 for unknown routes, serializes error responses as JSON, and logs internal errors. It does not decide which errors count as validation, not_found or conflict. That classification is delegated to the application-layer classifyError. The file contains no business rules, domain invariants or persistence logic, so every responsibility in it fits the infrastructure (transport adapter) role.
